source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U23: Apply the LLP agreement,defaults and partner-cessation consequences

payload.title: Partner exit does not erase accrued obligations
payload.core_explanation_md:
The LLP agreement governs the described mutual rights and duties; the First Schedule supplies the applicable defaults where it is silent. Changes require the prescribed filing. A pre-incorporation agreement needs the described all-partner ratification to impose its obligations on the incorporated LLP. Do not import an ordinary-firm deed rule without checking the LLP statute.

Cessation follows the agreement or the specified default written-notice route. The third party notice/Registrar notice rule matters to how a former partner is regarded in dealings. Cessation does not itself discharge obligations already incurred. The default capital/profit settlement entitlement does not give the former partner continuing management rights. Distinguish the exit date,the notice evidence,the settlement calculation and any separate guarantee.

self_check.prompt_text: Does resignation itself extinguish an earlier obligation?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Accrued obligations require their own discharge analysis.

payload.stem_md: A former partner demands management access solely because a capital settlement remains unpaid. What is the relevant distinction?

options.text_md: Unpaid settlement automatically restores all management power
Every exit extinguishes all financial rights
options.explanation_md: The source preserves a qualified entitlement.

options.text_md: The LLP ceases to exist when anyone resigns
Settlement entitlement and continuing management rights are different
options.explanation_md: The default exit framework does not confer interference rights.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The default exit framework does not confer interference rights.

options.explanation_md: The LLP has its own statutory default framework.
